body:
Found while verifying that #1750's forward fix is actually wired on merged main.
The wiring is correct. What it reaches is wider than the shipped plan said.

## What was promised

The plan the operator approved was "new books born split, no backfill, nothing
to orphan", on the measured basis that a book being converted for the first time
has no highlights yet. The CHANGELOG says "Books converted, uploaded, or
auto-ingested from now on".

## What the code actually does — OBSERVED on 9e06f0fa7

`cps/tasks/kepub_backfill.py` selects its work as:

    book_ids = [row[0] for row in
                app_session.query(ub.KoboSyncedBooks.book_id).distinct().all()]

That is **every book that has ever synced to a Kobo** — not new books. Each is
handed to `TaskConvert` (`_backfill_one_book`, kepub_backfill.py:141), which
computes, at `cps/tasks/convert.py:355`:

    may_split = not self._book_has_annotations() or (
        os.path.exists(destination) and package_was_split_by_us(destination))

For a backfill candidate the `.kepub` does not exist yet — that is why it is a
candidate — so the second clause is always False and the gate reduces to
`not self._book_has_annotations()`, which is **server-side annotations only**.

## Why that predicate is the wrong one, and it is already on record

F-a66189 and the 2026-08-18 reconnaissance measured that **11 of 30 device
bookmarks (37%) never reached the server**, concentrated in one book. So "no
server annotations" cannot distinguish *never highlighted* from *highlighted on
the device and the capture missed it*. That is exactly the reasoning used to
decouple the backfill from the forward fix — and this path applies the rejected
predicate anyway.

Blast radius, OBSERVED on the 41-book dev/reference library (NOT the operator's
production instance — that number is unmeasured):

    KoboSyncedBooks distinct book_id      43
    books with server annotations         19
    synced + has EPUB + no KEPUB           3   <- backfill candidates
      would be split (no server annots)    3
      withheld (has server annotations)    0

## What is NOT established, and it decides the severity

ASSUMED, not observed: that splitting makes these books *worse*. A candidate has
no KEPUB, so the device received an **EPUB**. The backfill creates a KEPUB, and
kepubify restructures the document (book-columns wrapper, koboSpans) whether or
not chapters are split. If the device re-downloads at all, existing device
highlights are already exposed by the format change; splitting adds renamed
spine documents on top of a change that was happening anyway.

Whether the device re-downloads **is F-3e383a**, still unmeasured.

## Consequence for F-3e383a's priority

F-3e383a is filed as deciding two designs in opposite directions. It decides
**three**. Add: whether the KEPUB backfill can split a Kobo-synced book without
risking device-side highlights.

  * device does NOT re-download on ChangedEntitlement -> this path is inert on
    already-synced devices, and the gate is cosmetic;
  * device DOES re-download -> the format change is already disruptive, and the
    split needs a gate that is not "no server annotations".

## Do not "fix" this by guessing

Tightening the gate to "never synced to a Kobo" would make the backfill select
nothing at all — `KoboSyncedBooks` IS the selection. Narrowing it needs the
measurement first. Filing rather than patching is deliberate.

--- SCOPE, 2026-08-20 (same day): it is not only a background migration ---

OBSERVED on fbfa9d4fc. A second entry point reaches the same gate, and this one
is on the REQUEST PATH:

`cps/helper.py:2358` in `get_download_link` — when a client asks for `kepub`,
`config_kobo_prefer_kepub` is on, and no KEPUB row exists:

    err = convert_book_format(book.id, config.get_book_path(),
                              'EPUB', 'KEPUB', None, blocking=True, timeout=25)

`convert_book_format` (`cps/helper.py:384`) constructs `TaskConvert(...)` and
enqueues it, so the on-demand conversion runs the identical
`may_split = not self._book_has_annotations() or (...)` gate.

So a Kobo asking to download a book whose KEPUB does not exist yet triggers a
split synchronously, at request time — not during a one-shot migration someone
chose to run. `is_kepub_backfill_pending()` only defers it while the startup
backfill holds the single-threaded worker; once that drains, the on-demand path
converts and splits.

This does not change the finding's open question (whether splitting makes these
books worse is still ASSUMED, and still gated on F-3e383a). It changes HOW OFTEN
and WHEN it can fire, which is what a severity judgement rests on.
title: The KEPUB backfill splits books that have already been on a Kobo, gated on a predicate that cannot see device highlights
